TL;DR There is a rigid school culture that values pretenses, vague promises and results on paper than the students’ wellbeing and joy for learning, choosing instead to reinforce conformity and the status quo. It is destructive to the uniqueness of students and teachers alike.  I was a Primary school student here from 2011-2016, and I’ve had both excellent and terrible teachers. Some genuinely care for their students, and are willing to go the extra mile for them to cultivate a joy for learning, but whether your child is taught by one of these passionate teachers is a game of dice.  Other teachers are mediocre, who view the job as nothing more than a requirement, and go into class to teach the bare minimum, and leave. There are a few, though, who are absolutely terrible - teachers ripping up worksheets, holding seven-year-olds by the collar and shouting in their faces for nothing more than literally stepping out of line - these are not uncommon sights. I’ve had teachers who yelled at some of my classmates, calling them “fat”, “stupid”, and other names. I’ve been told by a teacher that he “likes to cane students” as a scare tactic. Ironic, considering how much they constantly stress on the value of “leadership”.  Some leave students with lies for the purpose of achieving the school's goals, or to the benefit of their KPIs. The school’s pedagogy leaves innumerable things to be desired, creating a self-defeating educational milieu and choosing instead to conceal these shortcomings with a façade of values held up by nothing more than empty words. The environment in class is often no more than fear and resentment, and it’s no wonder that not a single student from the GEP graduating cohort of 2016 chose to return for secondary education.  There is much posturing and virtue-signalling about “character” and a “passion for learning” but nothing is done on the ground. I’ve spoken to teachers who hold genuine concern for the students, and even they feel constricted by the stifling environment. I’m not alone in my opinion, and I can say that I speak for the majority of my P6 class (they had a say in this review).  With all that said, I have no other primary school to compare Catholic High with, and I am not in the best position to critique it unbiasedly. However, many of my previous classmates have come from other primary schools and hold fondness for them, something that cannot be said for Catholic High.  Edit: grammar

This school is so underrated because it doesn’t go around blowing its own trumpet everywhere. I almost missed out on what FTPPS has to offer because I admittedly had doubts initially based on how it’s not the most thought of school in this area.  Some background- I transferred my middle son here from a Branded School because he was being bullied previously. Kheng Cheng was full and we didn’t try Pei Cun.  So we spoke to the teachers at First Toa Payoh and what struck me was the genuine care, concern and love for the kids I saw in the teaching staff. They communicate sincerely with parents too and are very constructive and supportive. It’s not just about hitting KPI here but the school aims to arm them with the right mindset and heart as well. They invested and paid to use materials from the kids version of seven habits of highly effective people to coach the kids growth mindset— the sort of lessons adults spend $1-2k to learn in a crash course. The principal and his teachers are patient and I’ve not encountered any teacher I’ve any particular disdain for like in the branded schools I’ve had experience with in the past.  The proof in the pudding is how my son will every once in a while chirp up, “I’m so glad you transferred me to this school.”  You see, the right school isn’t always the branded and top school. The right stream isn’t always GEP (don’t get me started on our experience). The right school is the one who connects with your child and makes them feel cared for, sparks a desire to learn and supports their emotional and mental development aside from their academics.  The right school is not the one that saves you face but that enables your child to learn happily in. A happy child is a good learner. A good learner will eventually blossom and do well.

I absolutely love this school and I would highly recommend it!  I was a student in this school from P2 all the way till P6. What I really like about HGS is that the teachers are really friendly and kind! They really care about the students, giving them less homework when it is a CCA day, lending a listening ear when they are stressed about exams, putting up extra study material to help them out on Google Classroom, and even organizing fun events to give them a break!  Besides that, HGS also sets aside time to teach students lessons that can't be learned in the classroom, like how to be leaders of character and practice the school values. HGS also invites students who excel at a particular area such as English or Art to take part in classes called "D3T2". This stands for "Discover, Develop and Dedicate your Talents & Time". In these classes, students learn how to better develop their talents, and in time, use them to serve their school and community. I've had a whale of a time in English Creative Writing D3T2, where my classmates and I wrote and discussed short stories, poems, and other works together. At the end of my P5 year, we even got to write a book for Kindergarten 2 students!  Of course, there are other reasons why my time here will be deeply etched in my mind, like the canteen's yummy food (especially the popcorn chicken in stall 2 nom nom), the wide variety of CCAs, and the talented students.  All in all, I'm really grateful I was in this school, and I'll really miss it. But, once a Haig Girl, always a Haig Girl 🤎💛🤍 Shoutouts to Mrs Celeste Lim (my amazing 6H form teacher), Ms Aisyah (my epic 4J form teacher), and Ms Yeo (my Creative Writing D3T2 teacher who is now in MOE HQ). Learning spaces are built-in to support broad-based and effective learning.  Classrooms are designed and equipped with a rich array of learning resources to cater to a range of learning approaches. The school is equipped with the following facilities to deliver quality programmes to the students:  • School Hall • Graffiti Wall • Indoor Sports Hall • Performing Arts Studio (in Media Resource Library) • School Playground • Outdoor Experiential Learning (OEL) Garden • Media Resource Library  The presence of such infrastructure provides opportunities for more holistic learning, tapping on the affordances of each specially selected facility being built. For instance, the OEL Garden is used for authentic experiential learning across different subjects. For Science, students can head to the garden to gain first-hand exposure to some of the different flora and fauna they learn in the textbooks. The school staff train all students to be independent from primary 1. By primary 2 they are already able to orientate new P1 students unsupervised (other sch use older P4 or P5 students). P1 students are taught how to write down instructions and homework just like other schools but by P3 they are already memorising what they need for the next days. Every school has enrichment courses that change yearly, normally 2 or 3 while Pei Tong offers 10-15 per year, no kidding. Bullying is not allowed and strict discipline protocol is in place that tackles the problem within 24h (other schools either don't care or procrastinate because overwhelmed with cases). Students after school are orderly, well behaved, and calm. Students of other schools are by contrast, running everywhere, unruly, swearing and screaming. You can really see the difference. Academic ability depends on the individual not the school but character building is best built from young and Pei Tong does a marvellous job. My child already graduated and is attending one of the top sec schools, scores A1 A2 in several subjects even without tuition there, doesn't take notes, everything memorised naturally in class, cool attitude no stress, thanks to training from Pei Tong, it saves us money!

In the end his PSLE results wasn't ideal. He performed even more badly compared to his prelims results.  And for the past 2 full years, his form teacher never even made an effort to follow up with me, not even once, even though I didn't request to meet up during Parents Meeting. But my friends whose kids are attending other schools feedback that the form teachers always follow up with them via whatsapp occasionally despite not attending the Parent's Meeting.  I really think this school, the higher management needs to buck up. I kind of regret sending my kid to this school. Should have apply for Compassvale Primary or Anchor Green Primary instead. A primary school which has a lovely  village feel and old-school caring community coupled with a modern, progressive teaching philosophy. It's no secret that Ang Mo Kio, its catchment area, has an ageing demographic and thus a declining number of primary school age children. Also no secret that TVPS is not a "brand-name" school. But these provide impetus for teachers and school leaders to work harder to attract students, and they certainly do. My daughter is studying there - while intellectually bright, she presents some behavioural problems in class. I have been very touched by how patient, empathetic, loving and dedicated her teachers and special education needs officers have been towards her. Not only that, but her classmates have mostly been very understanding and kind to her as well.  Another noteworthy point is the impressive diversity of the school population. Apart from the solid working-class and middle-class Chinese, Malay and Indian demographic of Ang Mo Kio, there is also an amazing array of children of other ethnicities - Eurasian/ European, numerous ASEAN countries, mainland Chinese and Indian immigrants, even Africans as the numerous non-Singaporean/PR kids living in the area are unable to enter the "popular" schools. Your child will get an international school-like cultural exposure here and learn how to relate to people of all backgrounds.
